fields.title: The fraud detection & streaming Analytics
fields.summary: Analyzes credit card transactions to identify potentially fraudulent activities using Python, MySQL, and Power BI
fields.problem: The project aimed to identify potentially fraudulent credit card transactions using transaction data and rule-based analysis, while reducing false positives and missed fraud cases.
fields.description:
1.Cleaned transaction data in Python.
2.Removed exact duplicate rows from the working dataset.
3.Applied two baseline rules: transaction amount greater than 100 and greater than 1,000.
4.Evaluated each rule against the dataset's Class label using true positives, false positives, false negatives, true negatives, precision, and recall.
5.Simulated batch-by-batch processing to demonstrate monitoring metrics.
6.Processed results in MySQL for analysis in Power BI.
Validate key counts across Python, MySQL, and Power BI.
fields.result: Tested two simple amount rules on 473 real fraud cases. Amount > 100 caught 26.43% of fraud (125 cases) but wrongly flagged 56,274 normal transactions. Amount > 1,000 wrongly flagged only 2,926, but caught just 1.90% of fraud (9 cases). Precision was very low for both (0.22% and 0.31%), showing that simple amount rules cannot reliably detect fraud and that better methods are needed.
